CORRECTION -- MY 'TRUSTED-MAIN ASYMMETRY' FRAMING IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE CARRIED FORWARD. The operator's test: if it were asymmetry, a rebase would fix it. It does not. I had the disconfirming evidence already and kept the label anyway -- change 2607 was branched from 6125c5345f01 ITSELF, the very commit that added the workflow, and still fails. That rules out anything a different base could cure.

WHAT ACTUALLY EXPLAINS HOW IT LANDED, and it is a stronger finding: the scanner-integration job NEVER RAN BEFORE MERGE. Change 2595's own Verified run (33831682168) contains 26 jobs -- lint, typecheck, four pytest matrix cells, artifact-probe, optionality, mutation shards, eval-discipline, pip-audit, golden-path, sandbox enforcement -- and NO scanner-integration job at all. It was granted Verified +1 without that job ever executing. Its first-ever execution was after it merged.

So this is not 'validated under conditions that did not match how it would later run'. It is ABSENCE OF COVERAGE: the job was never validated at all. That distinction matters because it changes AC3. The pre-merge gap to close is not 'detect behavioural divergence between lanes' but 'a newly added CI job must actually EXECUTE on the change that introduces it, or its Verified vote is vacuous'.

TWO QUESTIONS ARE NOW SEPARATE AND MUST NOT BE CONFLATED:
 (1) HOW did it land broken? Answered: the job did not run pre-merge, so nothing could have caught it.
 (2) WHY does it fail? STILL OPEN. 'Never ran before' explains the escape, not the fault.

For (2), what is RULED OUT: base staleness (2607's base is the workflow's own commit). What is NOT ruled out: the job may be broken outright on any tree, OR it may fail specifically for patchsets because every patchset is fetched as a refs/changes/* ref regardless of base -- a change-ref-vs-branch-ref difference would NOT be cured by rebasing either, so it survives the operator's test. Do not assume; measure.

DECISIVE EXPERIMENT NOW RUNNING. _scanner-integration.yml is a reusable workflow called from BOTH gerrit-verify.yaml:249 (patchsets) and test.yml:79 (branch head). test.yml is excluded from push-on-main and runs on a ~6-hourly schedule; the last scheduled run (33824556786, 01:07) PREDATES the merge and contains no scanner job, so it cannot answer this. I dispatched test.yml against main manually: run 33839813271. If scanner-integration PASSES there, the fault is specific to the patchset context, not the job. If it FAILS on main too, the job is simply broken and main is red right now.

SEPARATE CONFIRMED FINDING from the same run: that 01:07 scheduled main run failed on 'build-and-test / pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)' and 'sweep (windows)'. So bug 9a17 FAILS ON MAIN ITSELF, not only on patchsets -- worth recording on 9a17, since it means main's branch-head health is red independently of anything in review.

comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE EVIDENCE, found incidentally by the 9a17 agent before I stood down. Passing it over -- I am NOT working this ticket.

THE ACTUAL ERROR from a failing job log (change 2600, base 08a39c39c50d):
  python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/install_review_scanners.py':
  [Errno 2] No such file or directory
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

scripts/install_review_scanners.py arrived in 6125c5345f01. Verified absent on that change's base:
'git cat-file -e HEAD^:scripts/install_review_scanners.py' -> absent.

AND THE GUARD THAT EXISTS FOR THIS CLASS DOES NOT COVER IT: .github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml
is NOT in GUARDED_WORKFLOWS in tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py. That test's whole
purpose is to catch a CI step that cannot run on a tree predating it -- it caught exactly this shape
on change 2600 earlier today for a different step. The new workflow was simply never added to its
list. So the pre-merge detection gap is concrete and small: a hand-maintained list that the new
workflow was not added to.

That is the FIFTH instance today of the same meta-pattern -- a guard that exists but does not cover
the new case because its coverage is hand-registered rather than derived from the tree. The others:
740d (ticket 3476's bare-repo guard, hardcoded 3-file allowlist, missed a file added four days
later), the ADR .numbers collisions (marker created only at authoring time), c379 (ADR 0078 settled
container-vs-type and the scheduler never heard), and 2593 (hard-coded discovery-builder module list
that went stale when a split moved the code). Two of those were fixed by deriving coverage from the
tree instead of listing it; that is likely the durable shape here too.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT -- DO NOT LET THIS EXPLAIN MORE THAN IT DOES. The missing-file error accounts for
change 2600, whose base PREDATES the file. It does NOT obviously account for change 2607, which was
branched from 6125c5345f01 ITSELF, where scripts/install_review_scanners.py IS present, and which
still failed on scanner-integration. Either 2607 fails for a different reason, or something else
about the patchset context is involved. Worth confirming rather than assuming one cause covers both
-- I conflated two questions on this ticket once already.

Still free to read: dispatched run 33839813271 (test.yml against main) answers whether the job is
broken outright or only in the patchset context.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The `scanner-integration (pinned Semgrep + Gitleaks on the patchset)` job, added to `main` in
`6125c5345f01` (Gerrit change 2595, ticket aa9e), fails on every change pushed since it merged.
It casts `Verified -1` and blocks all merges; six open changes are affected (2594, 2600, 2601,
2607, 2608, 2609). With bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091` this leaves two gates red and no route to
`Verified +1`.

**How it landed broken (the escape).** The job never ran before merge. Change 2595's own
Verified run `33831682168` contains 26 jobs and no `scanner-integration` job at all: the
Verified lane executes `gerrit-verify.yaml` from trusted `main`, and `main` did not yet wire
the lane. So 2595's `Verified +1` was cast without the new job ever executing. Absence of
coverage, not divergent conditions — base staleness is ruled out (change 2607 is parented
directly on `6125c5345f01` and still fails).

**Why it fails (the fault) — two independent defects, both quoted from real job logs.**

Defect 1, the make recipe is not POSIX-sh portable. On a tree that carries the new script
(mirror branch-head lane, run 33834183836 job 100903189596, base `main`):

```
review scanner locks: OK
/bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
make: *** [Makefile:475: scanner-integration] Error 2
```

`Makefile:475` opens the recipe with `@set -euo pipefail;`. The Makefile sets no `SHELL`, so
GNU make runs recipes under `/bin/sh` — dash on ubuntu-latest, which has no `pipefail`. The
recipe contains no pipeline, so `pipefail` buys nothing. This breaks the job on main content
itself, independently of the patchset context.

Defect 2, the gate step is unguarded against a pre-gate base. Change 2608 (patchset
`f50dc100`, run 33837736047 job 100913937750):

```
python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/install_review_scanners.py':
[Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

`.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` runs `scripts/install_review_scanners.py` and
`make scanner-integration` with no `[ -f ]` guard and no `# predates-gate-ok:` marker — the
exact invariant `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` owns. That guard's
`GUARDED_WORKFLOWS` is a hardcoded tuple; `_scanner-integration.yml` (like `_artifact-probe.yml`
and `_eval-discipline.yml`) is wired into `gerrit-verify.yaml` but absent from the tuple, so the
completeness check never looked at it. A new lane is opt-in to its own invariant, which is
backwards.

## Approach

The pre-merge property to restore is that a newly added CI lane's correctness is enforced by
the **unit-test suite**, which always executes on the change that introduces it, rather than by
the new job, which does not. Both defects are made catchable that way, and the opt-in step that
2595 could skip is removed.

1. `Makefile` — replace `set -euo pipefail` with POSIX `set -eu` in the `scanner-integration`
   recipe. The recipe has no pipeline, so this is behaviour-preserving under bash and correct
   under dash.
2. `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` — wrap the gate step in the canonical
   `[ -f scripts/install_review_scanners.py ]` guard emitting the exact phrase
   `change predates the gate`, and make the failure path actionable: name the violated contract
   (pinned Semgrep + Gitleaks locks) and print the local reproduction command
   `make scanner-integration`.
3. `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` — derive `GUARDED_WORKFLOWS` from the lane
   instead of hardcoding it: take `gerrit-verify.yaml` and `test.yml` as roots and follow every
   local `uses: ./.github/...` reference transitively. A reusable workflow or composite action
   is then inside the invariant the moment it is wired, with no second edit. Keep the current
   tuple as an asserted floor so the derivation cannot silently shrink.
4. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — pin defect 1's class: every make recipe reachable
   from CI must parse under a strict POSIX shell, so a bash-only builtin fails in the local
   suite instead of on ubuntu-latest.

No new script, config key, env var, feature flag or lock is introduced, so the mechanism-delta
ratchet sees no new mechanism.

## Scope

- `Makefile` — the `scanner-integration` recipe's `set` line.
- `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` — guard plus actionable failure message.
- `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` — lane-derived guarded set, coverage assertion.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — POSIX-shell contract for make recipes.

## Testing

- Happy path: the scanner step is inside `test_completeness_every_gate_step_is_guarded_or_marked`
  and `test_empty_tree_every_guarded_step_skips_cleanly`; the guarded body run in an empty
  directory exits 0 and prints `change predates the gate`.
- Coverage path: a new assertion pins that the derived guarded set contains every local `uses:`
  target reachable from `gerrit-verify.yaml` and `test.yml`, so a future lane cannot be wired
  outside the invariant.
- Failure/edge path (defect-seeded RED): reintroduce each fault — drop the `-f` guard, and
  restore `set -euo pipefail` — and show the corresponding test fail, then revert.
- Empty/degenerate path: a recipe with no shell content passes the POSIX parse trivially rather
  than erroring.
- Verification set: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause is quoted from real job logs, not inferred from workflow source: both the
      `Illegal option -o pipefail` failure (job 100903189596) and the `No such file or
      directory` failure (job 100913937750) are cited with job ids. Checked by reading this
      description and the change's commit message.
- [ ] `scanner-integration` passes on a patchset that is otherwise unmodified relative to its
      base. Checked by this fix's Gerrit change reaching `Verified +1` with the
      `scanner-integration` job green.
- [ ] The escape is closed: a newly added CI lane can no longer land unvalidated because its own
      job did not execute on the introducing change. `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`
      derives its workflow set from the `gerrit-verify.yaml`/`test.yml` local-`uses:` closure
      rather than a hardcoded list, so the always-running unit suite covers a lane the moment it
      is wired; the make-recipe POSIX contract covers defect 1 the same way. Checked by running
      both modules and by the new coverage assertion failing when a lane member is omitted.
- [ ] Defect-seeded RED: with the guard removed the completeness test fails naming
      `_scanner-integration.yml`, and with `set -euo pipefail` restored the POSIX contract fails
      naming `scanner-integration`; both pass after revert. Checked by the quoted pytest output
      recorded in a ticket comment.
- [ ] The job's failure message names the violated contract and the local command that
      reproduces it. Checked by reading the step body: the failure path prints
      `make scanner-integration` as the local reproduction.
